Property: MDA-01 · RolesGuard doesn't unwrap request.user array
Description:
src/guards/roles.guard.ts reads request.user.roles directly. Passport actually sets request.user as a bare array ([userData]), set by src/auth/strategies/jwt.strategy.ts's validate(). An array has no .roles, so the guard's `if (!user.roles) return false` fires on every request — every @Roles(...)-protected route currently denies everyone, including real admins.
This blocks ALL admin-gated work: any new admin/super-admin dashboard route that uses @Roles('admin') will silently 403 real admins until this is fixed. Fix first, before building new admin-gated routes.
Acceptance Criteria:
Guard unwraps request.user[0] (or normalizes request.user once centrally) before reading .roles. Add a regression test asserting an admin with @Roles('admin') can access a protected route.
Confirm the 13 existing @Roles('admin') routes in zoom.controller.ts and the one in learner.profile.controller.ts:94 start working for real admins after the fix.
Verification Notes (verified Nov 4 2026): Confirmed live on feat/md_superadmin, 2026-11-04. Traced request.user's actual shape end-to-end: jwt.strategy.ts builds `const arr = [userData]; req.user = arr; return arr;`. roles.guard.ts never unwraps index 0. Verified this currently breaks all 13 @Roles('admin') routes in zoom.controller.ts.

Property: MDA-02 · super-admin controller has no role guard
Description:
src/super-admin/super-admin.controller.ts has no @UseGuards/@Roles/@RequirePermissions anywhere. Only the global JwtAuthGuard + OrgAuthorizationGuard apply — and OrgAuthorizationGuard short-circuits to true when no orgId is present in the request body (true for a bare {email} payload). Net effect: any authenticated user, including a student, can POST /super-admin with their own email and become super_admin in one request.
This is the exact surface a super-admin dashboard would extend — must be locked down before adding more super-admin UI/endpoints on top of it.
Acceptance Criteria: Add a real role/permission guard (@Roles('super_admin') once MDA-01 is fixed, or @RequirePermissions) to every route on this controller. Add a test asserting a non-super-admin gets 403.
Verification Notes (verified Nov 4 2026): Confirmed live on feat/md_superadmin, 2026-11-04. Read the controller class directly: no guard decorator at class or method level. Confirmed OrgAuthorizationGuard.extractOrgId finds nothing in a {email}-only body and short-circuits to true (org-authorization.guard.ts).

Property: MDA-21 · Recording upload step can't find its own merged file
Description: recording-worker.service.ts's resolveMergedFilePath merges a mentor session's Zoom recording segments into one file on local disk under temp-recordings/, then a later step (S3 or YouTube upload) looks for that exact file to ship it and throws 'Merged file not found' if it's gone. Acceptance Criteria: Either (a) make the merge-to-upload handoff resilient to a restart (re-merge from source segments if the local file is missing, rather than failing permanently), or (b) persist the merged file to durable storage (S3) immediately after merging, before attempting any further upload step, so a restart never loses it.

Property: MDA-27 · @RequirePermissions is never actually used anywhere — resource-level permission enforcement is dead
Description: Separate from MDA-03 (the two RBAC management controllers themselves being unguarded), this is a deeper issue in the enforcement path that's supposed to use zuvy_resources at the route level. PermissionsGuard (src/rbac/guards/permissions.guard.ts) is correctly wired onto 6 real controllers (bootcamp, batches, content, adminAssessment, instructor, mentor-slot instructor side) and does real org-membership / instructor-bootcamp-ownership checks there. But its fine-grained branch — `userHasPermissions(user.id, requiredPermissions, orgId)`, which joins zuvy_permissions to zuvy_resources to check a specific permission on a specific resource — only runs if a route has a non-empty `requiredPermissions` array, which only `@RequirePermissions(...)` can set (it's the only call site of `SetMetadata('permissions', ...)` anywhere). A repo-wide grep found every single usage of `@RequirePermissions(...)` across the entire codebase (in users.controller.ts, permissions.controller.ts, rbac.controller.ts) commented out, with zero exceptions. Net effect: the resource/permission-grained authorization check this whole RBAC system was built for has never fired on a single live request — every route that reaches this point gets `return true` at `permissions.guard.ts`'s `if (!requiredPermissions...)` branch. zuvy_resources is still genuinely used elsewhere (auth.service.ts's getFormattedPermissions queries it on every login/refresh/switchOrg to build the permissions map sent to the frontend) — but the backend route-level enforcement half of the system is dead.
Acceptance Criteria: Decide and re-enable @RequirePermissions(...) on the routes that actually need resource-level permission checks (likely the same routes currently relying only on the coarser org/role checks), uncommenting and verifying each one actually matches a real permission name seeded in zuvy_permissions/zuvy_resources. Add an integration test asserting a user without the required permission is rejected on at least one representative route, to prevent this silently regressing back to disabled again.
Verification Notes (verified Nov 4 2026): Personally verified by direct read, 2026-11-04. Confirmed the RequirePermissions decorator (src/rbac/decorators/require-permissions.decorator.ts) is the sole SetMetadata('permissions', ...) call site repo-wide. Grepped every @RequirePermissions( usage across src/ — all 6 matches found are commented out (users.controller.ts:112,167; permissions.controller.ts:50,396; rbac.controller.ts:68,413), zero active usages anywhere. Separately confirmed PermissionsGuard IS actively applied (uncommented @UseGuards) on 6 real controllers, so this is specifically the fine-grained-permission branch that's dead, not the guard itself. Cross-checked auth.service.ts's getFormattedPermissions to confirm zuvy_resources is still genuinely queried live via a different path (login/refresh/switchOrg).
